summary: Frontend-only QA of new currency + Smart Insight + Loan extra-payment features across all 6 calculators. Core math regressions all PASS. Smart Insight rendering and behavior all PASS. Loan extra-payment PASS. ONE CRITICAL BUG: currency selector on Discount/Loan does NOT visually change the currency symbol — all amounts still show '$' regardless of selection (EUR, INR, GBP, etc.). Root cause identified in money() fallback logic.

ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL: Changing the Currency select on /calculators/discount-calculator and /calculators/loan-calculator does NOT update any displayed monetary values — every amount continues to render with a hardcoded '$' symbol regardless of the selected currency (verified with EUR, INR — see screenshot: still '$60.00'/'$20.00'/'$80.00' after selecting EUR). Root cause: money() calls `new Intl.NumberFormat(navigator.language, {style:'currency', currency})`. In this preview browser (and any browser reporting a non-BCP-47 locale, e.g. Linux 'en-US@posix'), navigator.language = 'en-US@posix' causes Intl.NumberFormat to throw `RangeError: Invalid language tag: en-US@posix`. Confirmed via page.evaluate. The catch fallback then returns `"$" + n.toLocaleString(...)` — hardcoded '$' regardless of the currency arg, so EUR/INR/GBP/etc. all render as '$'. Fix: pass `undefined` (or a sanitized/whitelisted locale) as the first arg to Intl.NumberFormat so it uses the runtime default which handles the currency param correctly — e.g. `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, {style:'currency', currency}).format(n)`. Also fix the catch fallback so it does not hardcode '$' (use a symbol lookup or at least prefix with the currency code).

Cosmetic: Insight text for 40→52 shows multiplier as '1.3' instead of the '1.30' specified in the review. Cause: fmt() uses minimumFractionDigits: 0, so trailing zeros are trimmed. Not a math error, just a formatting nit.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix money() in components/calculator/impl/fields.tsx to not depend on navigator.language, which may be an invalid BCP-47 tag (e.g. Linux 'en-US@posix') and cause Intl.NumberFormat to throw. Recommended: `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { style: 'currency', currency }).format(n)` (browser uses its default resolved locale, which is BCP-47 safe). Also remove the hardcoded '$' in the catch fallback — fall back to a symbol lookup or `${currency} ${n.toFixed(2)}` so a fallback path never mislabels the currency.

MINOR: In percentage-calculator.tsx change-mode SmartInsight, either format the multiplier to always keep 2 decimals (`fmt(multiplier, 2)` with a minimumFractionDigits option, or use `multiplier.toFixed(2)`), so '1.3' renders as '1.30' as the spec requires.
critical_code_review_comments: money() fallback hardcodes '$' — silently misrepresents the currency whenever Intl.NumberFormat throws. Any exception path should still respect the `currency` parameter.

money() uses navigator.language directly without validating it is a valid BCP-47 tag. Robust code should pass `undefined` to Intl.NumberFormat (which uses the runtime's default and never throws on locale) or wrap in try/new Intl.Locale() to normalize first.

fmt(multiplier, 2) with default minimumFractionDigits: 0 loses trailing zeros. For 'exact 2 decimals' display cases (multipliers, percentages when strict), a dedicated helper or an explicit min-decimals arg would prevent regressions like '1.3' vs '1.30'.

context_for_next_testing_agent: After the money() fix is applied, only re-test the currency selector behavior on /calculators/discount-calculator and /calculators/loan-calculator: (a) selecting EUR should render '€60.00' (or locale equivalent), (b) selecting INR should render '₹' amounts, (c) reload persists selection and displayed symbol matches. No need to re-run other calculators — their core math and SmartInsight behavior are all confirmed working in this run. Env note: this preview browser reports navigator.language='en-US@posix' which is NOT a valid BCP-47 tag; that is the trigger for the current bug and is a realistic representative of some Linux user agents.
rca of the issue: Reproduction: 1) open https://globalcalc-inspect.preview.emergentagent.com/calculators/discount-calculator 2) enter price=80, discount=25 3) change Currency select to EUR. Expected: '€60.00' style amounts. Actual: still '$60.00', '$80.00', '$20.00'. RCA: In money() (components/calculator/impl/fields.tsx L206-220), `new Intl.NumberFormat(navigator.language, { style: 'currency', currency })` is called with navigator.language='en-US@posix' in this environment. That is not a valid BCP-47 language tag, so the constructor throws `RangeError: Invalid language tag: en-US@posix` (confirmed via page.evaluate). Control transfers to the catch, which returns `"$" + n.toLocaleString(...)` — the '$' is hardcoded and the `currency` arg is ignored. Fix: (a) drop navigator.language and pass `undefined` — `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, {style:'currency', currency}).format(n)` — the browser will use its default locale, which is always BCP-47 valid, and the currency symbol will follow the `currency` argument correctly. (b) Additionally, harden the catch branch so it never hardcodes '$' (e.g., use a small { USD:'$', EUR:'€', GBP:'£', INR:'₹', ... } symbol map, or prefix with the ISO code like `${currency} ${n.toFixed(2)}`).
